title: Three days in the river
hookLine: he walks into the river Bein to bathe and is not seen for three days

cards: Before dawn in Sultanpur. As he does every morning, the storekeeper walks down to the small river at the edge of town, the Bein, to bathe before the day begins. A servant waits on the bank with his clothes.
Nanak steps into the water, goes under, and doesn't come up. The servant waits. Shouts.
Runs for help. People come with ropes and nets; the governor himself, the story says, has the river searched. No body, no clothes, no trace.
By evening the town has decided he's drowned. His sister grieves. A day passes.

teach.b: First, plainly: nobody knows what happened in those three days. No hymn of Nanak's tells it. What there is comes from the janamsakhis, and Sikhs treasure it.

teach.h: A CUP OF AMRIT, AND A CHARGE.
teach.b: They say he was taken into the presence of God and given a cup of amrit, the nectar of immortality, and he drank it. He was sent back with a charge: go into the world, remember the Name, and teach others to remember it.
On the third morning he walked out of the river. Some tellings link this moment with the root verse from days ten and eleven; not every telling does.
Sikh tradition remembers the river as the place Nanak's mission began. What it was like from the inside, the sources leave in the water.

teach.h: A WEEK THAT BUILT TO THIS.
teach.b: Look at the week that led here: a baby born in Talwandi, a sister who saw first, a boy asking what the letters meant, a cobra's shade, a true bargain, a storekeeper saying tera.
All of it building, quietly, until one morning he walked into a river and came out someone the whole town would have to reckon with.
A gurdwara called Ber Sahib stands on the riverbank today, and tradition says the jujube tree there, the ber, is the one Nanak sat under.

how: Sikhs remember the Bein river as the place where Guru Nanak's mission began; pilgrims visit Gurdwara Ber Sahib in Sultanpur Lodhi and some bathe in the river.

games.q: you're the servant on the riverbank. the storekeeper went under and hasn't come up. what happens next, in the story?
o: he comes up a minute later, laughing.
the town searches and gives him up for drowned; three days later he walks out.
games.why: after three days, on the third morning, he walked out of the river, and the stories say he came back with a mission.

practice: Turn a tap to a thin, steady trickle, or sit by any running water, and listen. Bring to mind a time you went into something, a hard season, a loss, a long trip, and came out different.
You don't have to understand it; just let the water run.
